result.title: RubricAtlas: Mining Type-Level Rubrics from Expert Reports to Evaluate Deep Research Agents
result.summary: Deep research agents conduct multi-step Web searches and synthesise retrieved information into analytical reports. Evaluating these outputs requires checking which analyses they deliver, beyond the presence of relevant facts. Query-specific binary rubrics make individual requirements explicit, but task-level checklists may leave the overall analytical structure underexamined. We introduce RubricAtlas, which derives type-level analytical requirements from expert reports on different objects within the same research type and organises detailed checks around recurring analytical questions. The requirements give related tasks a shared standard for what to analyse, without prescribing their answers. Our framework links binary checkpoints to report passages and evaluates completeness separately from argument validity. Built from 3,079 Chinese financial research reports, RubricAtlas covers 99 research types. Reference-report selection experiments show that individual reports cover only about half of their type's analytical questions, and that selecting requirements from different reports changes evaluation scores and agent rankings. Across ten agents, two judge pipelines achieve checkpoint agreement of $κ$ = 0.71 and agent-ranking agreement of Kendall $τ$ = 0.87. Controlled deletions reduce scores on the affected analyses, while padding produces no detectable increase. These findings support type-level rubrics for comparing the analytical completeness of Web deep research outputs, with individual decisions traceable to report evidence.

AI.brief_summary: RubricAtlas 从 3,079 篇中文金融研报中挖掘同一研究类型下共享的「类型级」分析要求，将细粒度二元检查点与报告段落对齐，并把完整性评价与论证有效性分开，用于比较十个深度研究 agent 的分析覆盖度与排序稳定性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「检查点—证据段落」可溯源对齐及完整性/有效性分离的评价设计，可能可供核查用于衡量 latent 推理轨迹对视觉证据的覆盖与贡献分配，但纯文本 Web 场景与视觉状态生成无直接联系。
